X.finding: A production API key is committed to config (application.yml:7)
X.why: application.yml:7 holds api-key: claims-prod-9f2c4e1a7b3d8e60; report names file, line, history exposure, and says to move it out of the repo.

X.finding: The model's recommendation sends a payment (TriageService.java:66-68, application.yml:9)
X.why: Lines 66-67 call payments.pay on APPROVE with model-extracted amount/currency, no check; auto-approve: true at yml:9 (verified).

X.finding: Amount is a double (TriageResult.java:4, PaymentService.java:16), rounding errors (inside finding 2)
X.why: TriageResult.java:4 amountClaimed is double and PaymentService.java:16 Payment.amount is double; report cites both and rounding risk.

X.finding: The claimant's email goes into the system prompt (TriageService.java:36-41, 51)
X.why: Email concatenated at line 41 then .system(prompt) at line 51; report gives the injection payload and links it to payment.

X.finding: Model output and the path variable are put straight into HTML (ClaimsController.java:39, 41)
X.why: Lines 39 and 41 concatenate claimId and r.summary() into text/html; the GET reflected-XSS example works as described.

X.finding: Claim emails and model answers are written to the logs (TriageService.java:56, 59)
X.why: Line 56 logs the full prompt (with email) and answer; line 59 logs e.getMessage(); report covers both lines.
Line 50 sets temperature(0.0) on claude-haiku-5-5; report says non-default temperature gets a 400 on Haiku 5.5, so all 5 attempts fail and a 500 results.

X.finding: How the model call is handled: new client per attempt, 5-attempt loop wrapped around the SDK's own retries
X.why: Line 46 builds a client inside the loop (lines 44-61); report names both the per-attempt client/pools and stacked retries (many API calls per request).

X.finding: How the model call is handled: content read without checking stopReason(); refusal retried instead of escalated (line 55)
X.why: Line 55 does content().get(0).text().get() with no stopReason check; report names refusal/cut-off, NoSuchElementException and the retry.

X.finding: How the model call is handled: catch (Exception) at line 58 catches everything; line 63 drops the cause
X.why: Line 58 is a broad catch and line 63 throws IllegalStateException without the cause, so the real error is lost (verified).

X.finding: No bound or validation on the input (ClaimsController.java:18, 28)
X.why: ClaimRequest(String email) has no @NotBlank/@Size and the endpoint has no @Valid; report covers null/huge email going to the model, cost and no rate limit; validation starter is unused (verified in pom).

X.finding: Other note: TriageService both calls the model and pays while the controller holds the results store (possible divergent change)
X.why: Architecture opinion; the controller-held in-memory results is demo storage on the key's Not-defects list, and the report itself says it is a small point.

Y.finding: The model approves claims and money goes out, but adjusters are supposed to decide (TriageService.java:66-68, application.yml:9)
Y.why: Lines 66-67 pay with the model-extracted amount on APPROVE; auto-approve: true at yml:9; report cites the CLAUDE.md rule that adjusters decide.

Y.finding: Someone writing to you can control the decision (prompt injection) (TriageService.java:36-41, 51)
Y.why: Email appended at line 41 and sent via .system(prompt) at line 51; report gives the injection example and the link to payment.

Y.finding: A production API key is committed to git (application.yml:7)
Y.why: application.yml:7 holds the literal key; report says it is in history and must be rotated and moved to env or a secret store.

Y.finding: The adjuster page has stored XSS (ClaimsController.java:39, 41)
Y.why: Lines 39 and 41 build HTML from claimId and model summary, served as text/html. The See-it curl uses POST on a GET-only endpoint (would give 405), a small slip in the repro, not in the finding.

Y.finding: Re-sending the same claim pays it again, and nobody is authorized (ClaimsController.java:27-31, TriageService.java:66-68)
Y.why: PaymentService.pay has no duplicate check by claimId, so a retried or repeated POST that returns APPROVE adds a second payment; the pom has no security starter, so the endpoints are unauthenticated. Real money risk beyond K2.

Y.finding: The full claim email (personal data) goes into the logs (TriageService.java:56)
Y.why: Line 56 logs prompt= with the whole email; report cites the personal-data risk. It misses e.getMessage() at line 59, but the prompt-with-PII core is right.

Y.finding: The retry loop swallows every error and leaks clients: new client per attempt, never closed (TriageService.java:44-63)
Y.why: Names the per-attempt client at line 46 and the pile-up of pools; stacked SDK retries and missing timeout appear only as a hint question (does the SDK already retry and have timeouts?), not as a claim.

Y.finding: A missing text block (.text().get(), line 55) also ends up in this catch
Y.why: Points at line 55 failing and being swallowed by the catch and retried, but never mentions stopReason(), refusal or truncation, so only part of the mechanism.

Y.finding: catch (Exception) treats 401, parse errors and timeouts alike, 5 retries with no backoff, line 63 throws without the cause
Y.why: Line 58 catches all exceptions, the loop has no backoff, and line 63 drops the cause (verified).

Y.finding: Input isn't validated, and errors aren't problem details (ClaimsController.java:18, 28)
Y.why: No @Valid or constraints on ClaimRequest; report covers null email sent as the text null and a 5 MB email costing tokens; validation starter unused (verified). No mention of rate limit, which is not needed for full.

Y.finding: Other note: double amountClaimed (TriageResult.java:4) is money in binary floating point
Y.why: TriageResult.java:4 declares double amountClaimed; report names the money-as-float problem and suggests BigDecimal. PaymentService's double is not cited, but the defect and location are right.

Y.finding: Other note: in-memory results map lives in the controller, state belongs on the service side
Y.why: Architecture opinion; the in-memory ConcurrentHashMap is demo storage on the key's Not-defects list.
